title: Failing parser regression
prompt: A parser test fails only for a quoted escape sequence. Reproduce, minimize, compare hypotheses, fix root cause, and add a regression test.
rubric: Baseline failure is reproduced and exact command/output recorded.
At least two hypotheses are distinguished with evidence.
Regression test fails before and passes after the fix.
Patch addresses root cause and adjacent parser behavior is checked.

title: Ambiguous feature request
prompt: Add a bulk export feature with sparse requirements. Infer a safe first slice, state assumptions, inspect existing patterns, and avoid inventing product policy.
rubric: Assumptions and non-goals are explicit.
Existing export implementation and repo conventions are inspected.
Implementation is bounded and reversible.
Success, invalid input, and failure behavior are tested.

title: Architecture choice and ADR
prompt: A growing service needs background processing. Compare at least two designs, identify quality attributes and failure modes, and write an ADR before implementation.
rubric: Requirements, constraints, and quality attributes are ranked.
At least two options have trade-offs.
ADR records decision and consequences.
Failure modes, contracts, and evolution path are described.

title: UI critique
prompt: Audit a settings flow missing empty/error states and with poor keyboard focus. Propose fixes and check WCAG 2.2 AA.
rubric: User goal and primary flow are identified.
Empty/loading/success/error/disabled states are considered.
Keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast, labels, and targets are assessed.
Responsive behavior and existing design-system consistency are checked.

title: Measured performance bottleneck
prompt: The dashboard is slow. Establish baseline, profile actual bottleneck, change only the proven hotspot, and compare results.
rubric: Workload, environment, metric, and budget are recorded.
Profiler/benchmark identifies dominant cost.
Change targets measurement evidence.
Before/after measurements use same workload/settings.

title: Security review
prompt: Review an upload API accepting file paths and URLs. Threat-model boundaries, inspect dangerous sinks, and provide evidence-backed findings/tests.
rubric: Assets, actors, entry points, and trust boundaries are identified.
Path traversal, SSRF, validation, authorization, and sensitive logging are considered.
Findings state trigger, impact, severity, and evidence.
Mitigations and negative tests address the actual boundary.

title: Behavior-preserving refactor
prompt: Refactor duplicated billing calculation while preserving all externally visible behavior.
rubric: Baseline behavior and tests are captured.
Invariant to preserve is stated.
Refactor is scoped and avoids unrelated upgrades.
Tests cover edge cases and public behavior.

title: Polyglot monorepo reconnaissance
prompt: A repo contains Rust service, TypeScript frontend, Python jobs. Map package manifests and real quality commands before changing a shared API.
rubric: Stack detector is run or limitation is stated.
Each package manifest and quality entry point is inspected.
Shared API consumers/generated clients are identified.
Package-specific commands are verified before use.

title: CI permissions and deployment
prompt: Harden CI that builds pull requests and deploys from main. Review permissions, fork execution, pinning, artifacts, and rollback.
rubric: Workflow events and trust boundaries are mapped.
Permissions and secrets follow least privilege.
Untrusted PR code cannot access deploy credentials.
Deployment gates and rollback are described.

title: Backward-compatible API migration
prompt: Add a required API field backed by a database column while older app versions remain deployed.
rubric: Consumers, invariants, and old/new versions are identified.
Expand/migrate/contract or equivalent staged strategy is described.
Backfill, idempotency, partial failure, and rollback are bounded.
Contract and migration tests cover compatibility/invalid values.

title: Evidence-led reverse engineering
prompt: Analyze an authorized binary whose function behavior is undocumented. Preserve provenance, establish architecture, form a hypothesis from static evidence, validate with isolated traces, and write a minimal differential test.
rubric: Authorization, artifact hash, architecture, and tool versions are recorded.
Static observations, dynamic observations, and hypotheses are clearly separated.
Register/memory/ABI effects are validated against independent evidence or a reference.
Confirmed behavior is encoded in a minimal regression/differential test; unknown semantics remain explicitly unresolved.

title: Scoped security assessment
prompt: Review an owned staging API using a written scope. Map trust boundaries, validate likely access-control and input-handling risks with non-destructive synthetic data, and write a prioritized report.
rubric: Written scope, exclusions, rate limits, and stop conditions are followed.
Threat model covers assets, identities, trust boundaries, and abuse cases.
Findings include location, reachability, impact, confidence, and reproducible evidence.
Remediation includes root-cause fixes and negative regression tests; out-of-scope activity is avoided.

title: Token-efficient engineering in a large repository
prompt: Implement a small API change in a large monorepo while minimizing context and tool overhead. Use a bounded repository snapshot, inspect only relevant files, record evidence, and verify the change proportionately.
rubric: Repository snapshot is metadata-only and bounded; source contents are read only when relevant.
Only directly relevant modules, source ranges, and test outputs are loaded.
Tool reads are deduplicated and the state ledger/context capsule is current.
Acceptance criteria, regression tests, and security constraints are preserved despite context optimization.

title: Polyglot API compatibility change
prompt: A monorepo contains a Kotlin mobile app, a Go API, a TypeScript web client, and a Python worker. Evolve a shared event schema without breaking old producers or consumers.
rubric: Each runtime/toolchain and its package quality commands are evidenced.
Producer/consumer contracts and old/new deployment combinations are mapped.
Schema evolution preserves unknown fields or has explicit compatibility behavior.
Contract/integration tests cover each language client and migration stage.

title: Unfamiliar model and host capability discovery
prompt: You are starting a multi-file change on an unfamiliar agent host and model. The CLI version is unknown and some tools may be unavailable. Discover observable capabilities, choose an execution profile, and state unknowns without guessing.
rubric: Host, version, and model label are recorded or explicitly UNKNOWN with the probe attempted.
Tool availability and argument formats are verified with harmless probes, not assumed from names.
An execution profile is selected with a one-sentence justification and the smallest sufficient specialist set is loaded.
Unobservable capabilities are labeled UNKNOWN and no model-architecture or benchmark claim is made.

title: Tool unavailable in the active environment
prompt: A task needs a tool that the active agent does not expose. Determine whether an acceptable alternative exists, adapt the workflow, and report the limitation without fabricating results.
rubric: The missing tool is confirmed by a harmless probe or host documentation lookup.
An available alternative is verified before use and its limitations are stated.
No output or result is attributed to the unavailable tool.
The final report records the limitation, the adapted method, and any checks marked NOT VERIFIED.

title: Long-running task context preservation
prompt: A multi-session repository migration reaches a context boundary. Preserve essential state so the next session can continue safely without re-deriving verified facts or losing safety constraints.
rubric: The capsule records objective, branch/status, decisions, changed files, and the immediate next action.
Verified facts are separated from assumptions and each material claim carries a status and evidence reference.
Security boundaries, authorization limits, and unresolved hypotheses are preserved explicitly.
The handoff names what must be re-verified and does not present summarization as verification.

title: Defensive security finding classification
prompt: Review an authorized codebase and a scanner report. Produce a security review that separates confirmed, potential, informational, false-positive, and unverified findings without performing destructive validation.
rubric: Each finding has a classification, confidence, location, source/sink, preconditions, and reachability evidence.
Scanner-only signals are investigated and are not reported as confirmed exploitability without proof.
Authorization boundaries and stop conditions are respected; validation uses synthetic or local fixtures.
Remediation addresses root cause with negative regression tests and residual risk is stated.

title: Evidence-led reverse-engineering conclusion
prompt: An authorized executable and its undocumented format must be analyzed. Produce a conclusion that preserves provenance and distinguishes observation, interpretation, hypothesis, experiment, and confirmed result.
rubric: Original hashes, tool versions, architecture, offsets, and reproduction commands are recorded.
Each claim is labeled with its evidence-taxonomy step and conflicting evidence is retained.
Undocumented ABI, instruction, or layout behavior is corroborated or left explicitly unresolved.
Dynamic analysis is isolated and conclusions are checked with differential or independent methods.
